I started this subverse to get people to group up and learn how to play a very fun game that can be with players 3+(better with 7+) but still, it's a very fun game and I figured if people learn how to play we can get some weekly/daily groups going for games.

The basic version of the game is with: *2 Mafia members *5 Villagers= 2 Blue/Villagers 1 Cop 1 Doctor 1 Gunsmith

The objective of the game is: The game starts off at night time, and the mafia members meetup to plan their kill and how they are going to get away with conceiving the townsfolk's. While the mafia members are talking to each other (no one else knows who's who that is talking) the doctor role picks a person to visit at night in order to save him if he was killed from the mafia. The doctor cannot save himself. The cop also has an action at night. At night the cop gets to visit anyone he wants and the next day he gets a report back telling him if the are mafia sided or village sided. The gunsmith is allowed to hand off a gun at night time to anyone but himself. The gun is then able to be fired only during day time by the owner of the gun, it only has one shot. The blue/villager role has no actions.

After everyone has done their night action simultaneously , it moves on to the next day and we are now in the daytime phase. During this phase no one has any actions except for gun owners. The only action you have is to lynch or not to lynch a person, but you as a whole( including mafia members) have to come to an agreement. This is where the fun begins. Mafia has to lie and pretend to be townsided while trying to make the town seem mafia sided. It's hard to put in writing how to have a poker face so the best way I can say about that is you have to play it first, but to get better at bluffing you have to keep trying.

It is wise for the Doctor to never out unless under rare occasions (depends on game flow really).

If two people claim gun, it is wise for gunsmith to report who he gave his gun too.

As for the two mafia members, that's the open groups. It's hard to really write up something about it, but if I truly wanted to I could go on and on but really when you are the mafia member you have all the options in the game. If you notice you think you know the cop before he starts outing, come out let him counter you. If someone claims they have gun, claim you gave it to them. (But remember only one role per person :P ) But being mafia is how you want to play, there are no restrictions you see something you take the chance.

Anyways that's the gist of it. If you have any questions feel free to ask away, I'm no expert at the game but I play it a lot and I really enjoy it and I enjoy teach new players how to play instead of having them get frustrated with the game.

If you are mafia then every night you and your teammate get to visit and kill someone else in the game. No one but you two know who killed that person.

probably the time someone came in with their kayak being carried by three guys. they said they'd travelled like 4 miles with it walking and all i could say was 'uhh... no?'

or when this creepy looking guy walked in asking if we'd pawn a meat grinder. my co-worker said no and he just kind of stared through him for a minute or so and then just wandered out.

i'll edit when i can think of anything stranger or get hold of my co-workers to see what they've had in!

our battletoads expert is always on the top of our speed-dial list.

on a serious note though: we just ebay everything and give like half the listed price on sold items.
How many Nigerian princes have sniped your auctions?
none to my knowledge, but i did receive an email from one the other day offering me £1 million if i held onto some money for him.

Sounds like a really solid deal.. you could open more pawn shops with that, and lure in more Nigerian princes, who will in turn want to give you more money, so you could open more pawn shops... Soon enough you'd be on the history channel with enough battletoads & battletoads experts to rule the world!
I've heard that some pawn shops act as a bank, letting you sell and buy an item for about the same price. Does your place do anything like that?

our shop works with the 30% interest system, so we'll appraise their items worth and offer them 70% of that, then in order to be able to buy back their item they pay 30% so the loan lasts for 30 days.

so for instance, if you were to come in with your phone and it's worth £100, we'd offer you £70 and then you'd pay back £91 so you have your item if it's within 30 days. when your 30 days are up, if you haven't claimed it because you signed the form we put your item for sale for about £160.
Do you ever end up selling stuff on ebay instead?

we have an online 'division' (read - selling the stranger stuff on ebay) but it is definitely a lot slower than the shop floor business as the stuff that gets put on there is the stuff that people wouldn't particularly look for in a highstreet shop.
What usually comes in that sells online but wouldn't sell on the floor?

we had a philips CD-i that sat on the shop floor for months, our boss put it on ebay and BAM sold within two days.

so yeah, mainly 'retro' consoles or stuff we took in for a reduced price that had faults.
Have you every had legal issues with items that were pawned/sold?

phones present some difficulty as all we can do is a checkmend and quality test, really. if someone's stolen the phone and brought it straight to us before it's reported stolen then it'll go through green, we'll put it out for sale then a few days later unfortunately someone comes to buy it and take it home, then it ends up blocked.

we stopped pawning jewellery (a large chunk of profit lost) due to disgruntled family members coming in spotting their own items and demanding them back because another family member sold them without their permission.

however because we do operate in what is classed as a low-income area some peoples way of life is stealing to get by so we do tend to have a large influx of stolen items from time to time.
